# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural issue with his heart that the doctors are monitoring. 
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation and struggles to go to the bathroom regularly, causing him distress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems clumsy, often tripping or stumbling when running or playing, which could be related to coordination issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have difficulties with coordination and balance.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, often turning the TV volume up high to hear clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which makes it hard for him to see clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are prone to problems, requiring more frequent dental visits to keep them healthy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in individuals with KBG syndrome, and regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with shorter fingers than usual, which sometimes makes it tricky for him to hold onto things or do certain tasks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental problems
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing and address any hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor and address any vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor the structural heart issue
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address coordination issues and developmental delays
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider review and investigation for tethered cord if clinical concerns arise
* Regular monitoring of the patient's heart condition and adjustment of treatment as necessary

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural abnormality in his heart, which is being monitored through regular check-ups to ensure it does not significantly impact his daily life.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery and others needing monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gains weight slowly compared to his peers, although he eats well and does not show signs of discomfort after eating.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A very small number of children have required longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with a tethered cord, which could potentially affect his development, and he has scoliosis, for which he is undergoing physical therapy to improve his posture and reduce the curvature of his spine.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis). Tethered cord, affecting spinal cord movement, has been found in about 11% of children with KBG syndrome.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has times when he doesn't respond right away to his name being called, suggesting potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to sit very close to the TV or leans in close when looking at pictures, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint. Regular eyesight reviews are recommended.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of tooth sensitivity when eating cold foods, which started a few months ago and has been consistent since then.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Besides large front teeth, people with KBG syndrome can have weak enamel, making regular dental check-ups important. Other dental concerns can include a variety of issues requiring specialist care.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay and behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis and was born with a tethered cord.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly), and a small number have hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and other potential dental issues.
* Hearing reviews to assess and address any hearing loss or concerns.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to check for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint.
* Regular monitoring of the heart condition to ensure it does not worsen.
* Physical therapy to manage scoliosis and improve posture.
* Consideration of referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any skeletal abnormalities.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and manage any delays or difficulties.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient appears to get tired more quickly than other kids her age, which can be concerning at times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A study of 40 European patients showed that 15/40 (38%) had heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Mealtimes have often been a struggle for her, with certain foods she can't tolerate well and digestive issues popping up now and then.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy and has to take medication daily to control her seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people are reported as having seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had a glue ear recently, which was a bit of a challenge to deal with.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs her eyes quite frequently, especially when she's trying to focus on something, and it's almost like she's having trouble concentrating or her eyes get tired easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem to break or chip very easily, and she needs to be super careful with what she eats to avoid damaging them further.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has short fingers on one hand and also scoliosis, which require regular monitoring and occasional physiotherapy sessions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent damage
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor for vision problems
* Consider a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) to monitor for heart conditions
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor for skeletal anomalies
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and manage symptoms.

Parent: Our daughter has a bit of a problem with her eyes, specifically she has hypermetropia, which means she has trouble seeing things up close. She holds books really close to her face to read.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Sometimes she asks us to repeat ourselves because she didn't quite catch what we said the first time. It's like she needs a little extra help to understand.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her teeth are a concern; the dentist mentioned that the enamel is weak. We're working on making sure she brushes them gently and regularly.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Physically, she can't keep going for very long without getting tired. Simple games like tag or running around exhaust her quicker than her friends.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Now and then, she'll just stare off into space for a few seconds. It's unnerving at first, but it happens often enough that we've learned to recognize it and make sure she's okay afterward.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Food wise, she's extremely picky about textures. Some foods she just won't touch if they have the wrong feel. Mealtime can be challenging because of this.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Two other things - her fontanelle took longer than usual to close, and there are these palatal abnormalities we're keeping an eye on. The specialists are monitoring both closely.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences physical exhaustion more quickly than her peers, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is extremely picky about food textures, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient occasionally stares off into space for a few seconds, which is concerning but recognized by the parents.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes asks for repetitions due to difficulty hearing, indicating potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, trouble seeing things up close, and holds books very close to her face to read.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel, and the dentist has advised gentle and regular brushing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth and may experience other dental concerns, including weak enamel.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's fontanelle took longer than usual to close, and there are palatal abnormalities being monitored.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address weak enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to assess and manage potential hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct and manage hypermetropia
* Consider a cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess cardiac function
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental needs
* Regular monitoring of palatal abnormalities and adjustment of feeding strategies as necessary
* Consider review and investigation for tethered cord if clinical concerns arise

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had a glue ear before, which was due to a buildup of fluid, and the parent is aware of the need for preventive measures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs his eyes a lot when trying to focus, indicating potential trouble seeing clearly, and there are concerns about his eye health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired easily when playing with friends or running around and has difficulty keeping up with other kids during physical activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has some issues with her bowels.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems a bit clumsy sometimes, and her coordination isn't as good as some of the other children her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: There's been some fluid buildup in her ears, and she has trouble hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things that are far away, like the board in her classroom.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to go to the dentist pretty often due to some issues that keep coming up with her teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient moves around differently than the other kids, and her coordination isn't as good as some of the other children her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may experience developmental delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some may have short fingers or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth issues
* Regular hearing reviews to address the fluid buildup in her ears and potential hearing loss
* Eyesight review to correct her vision problems
* Cardiac review to investigate the cause of her tiredness and difficulty keeping up with physical activities
* Referral for a skeletal review to check for any spinal or hip issues
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address her coordination and developmental issues

Parent: Our child has hypermetropia, which means he has a higher-than-normal curvature of the cornea. This causes him to have blurry vision at times and can make focusing a challenge.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, our son had glue ear when he was younger. It caused some discomfort and affected his ability to hear clearly for a period. Thankfully, after treatment‚ it cleared up and he's back to normal now.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: One thing we've noticed is that our child has rather large front teeth compared to other kids his age. They seem a bit protruded‚ but we aren't sure if this will cause any long-term orthodontic issues.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: What we'v observed is that our child gets tired more easily than his peers. He might not be able to sustain physical activity over long periods like running around in the playground. 

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves‚ muscle tone‚ fits).
Parent: There was an issue detected related to the tethered cord‚ but the neurosurgeons are keeping a close watch on it to see how it develops and whether it'll need intervention later on.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more easily than peers and may not be able to sustain physical activity over long periods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty swallowing, especially with thicker textures, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord, which may cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, and an unusual gait.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have difficulty with neurological development.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear when younger, which caused discomfort and affected hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, causing blurry vision at times and making focusing a challenge.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth, which seem protruded.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have large permanent teeth, and some may have weak enamel or other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder or ADHD.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a slightly different posture when standing or walking, almost as if favoring one side over the other.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual structure of the spinal bones, short fingers, or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth development and enamel health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor for skeletal anomalies
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and address any delays or difficulties.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks people to repeat themselves, indicating possible hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when looking at things, especially in bright light, suggesting possible vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with some requiring patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural heart problem.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties and trouble eating.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was slow to walk and sit, and took time to get it right.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, and around 20-40% of people are reported as having seizures.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing problems and turns the TV up high to hear, and also has a squint.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and many children have required multiple aeration tube insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints and has vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and the extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a bad hip and palatal abnormalities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many people have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5
* Eyesight review to monitor vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor heart condition
* Consider a skeletal review to monitor spinal and hip problems
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and behaviour
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect, which is an opening in the wall between the two upper chambers of the heart. 
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences frustration during mealtimes if the food isn't just right or if he's not hungry at the exact moment, making mealtime stressful.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient occasionally has episodes where he stares off into space and seems completely unresponsive for a few seconds.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, of varying types.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often turns the volume of the TV up very high, indicating potential trouble hearing softer sounds.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes squints when looking at things, which can make his eyes get a bit tired, especially when trying to focus on something close up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods like meats or tough vegetables due to teeth or jaw pain.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's speech development has been slower than expected, and he doesn't speak as much or as clearly as other kids in his class.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has slower speech development and experiences frustration during mealtimes, indicating potential behavioral differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has slightly different coordination and balance, affecting how he plays and interacts physically.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and jaw health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address potential hearing concerns
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess bone health
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and address behavioral differences

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing when playing or running around, which is being monitored.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets faster than expected when engaged in physical activities, and there are concerns about potential heart issues that need monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had feeding difficulties as a baby, including trouble latching on and getting full quickly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires easily from physical activities and has shorter endurance than peers, suggesting potential neurological impacts.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is bothered by loud noises, gets frustrated and overwhelmed in crowded or noisy spaces, and has had issues with hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often rubs his eyes, especially when trying to focus, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had dental issues requiring frequent dentist visits and attention.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups, especially with a specialist SEN dentist for those with significant sensory issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which may require medication or other interventions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably shorter fingers than average and an off posture when standing or walking, which could affect his back or overall comfort.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers (brachydactyly), curved 5th fingers (clinodactyly), and an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), with some experiencing delayed closure of the soft spot on the head or hip dysplasia.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental health issues.
* Regular hearing reviews, especially in the first few years, to identify and manage any hearing concerns.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and correct any vision problems.
* Consideration of a cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to evaluate heart health.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with potential referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and address specific challenges.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart valve problem.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulties during mealtime and gets upset.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia (low muscle tone) and struggles with speech, making it hard to understand him when he tries to speak.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, hearing some noises but not all.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia (nearsightedness) and cannot see far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have large permanent upper middle teeth (macrodontia of upper central incisors) and may have weak enamel, requiring regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with speech and has difficulties during mealtime.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers (brachydactyly), curved 5th fingers (clinodactyly), and an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor vision problems
* Cardiac review (including echo and ECG) to monitor heart conditions
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor skeletal anomalies
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and address difficulties.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord issue, which has caused concerns about his movement and coordination. He also has scoliosis, affecting his posture and requiring regular exercises.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had glue ear, affecting his hearing temporarily. He has also had issues with his teeth, including larger than usual front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss. Many children require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, with his eyes slightly turned inward, requiring special glasses to correct.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint. Treatment can include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has larger than usual front teeth, which the dentist is monitoring to prevent further issues with his bite or speech.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important. Regular dental check-ups are essential, especially for those with significant sensory issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school. Some may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety. Medication may be appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, affecting his posture and requiring regular exercises.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to increased curvature of the spine. Many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers, and some have hip dysplasia.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had issues with otitis media, an ear infection that keeps coming back, but antibiotics usually clear it up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia (long-sightedness) and uses glasses to correct her vision.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing than typical for kids his age when playing actively.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets faster than what's typical for kids his age when playing actively, and a cardiologist is monitoring the situation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, often showing disinterest in food or struggling to swallow certain textures, and works closely with a nutritionist to find comfortable foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone, making him feel stiffer than usual and impacting movement.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has fluid buildup in his ear that affects his ability to hear clearly at times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which affects how he sees things and sometimes causes headaches.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has sensitive teeth, particularly to cold foods and drinks, due to sensitive nerves.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and some have large front teeth and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeable speech delays and developmental concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delays.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor ear fluid buildup and hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor hypermetropia and other vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor heart condition and breathing
* Speech therapy to address speech delays and developmental concerns
* Occupational therapy to address feeding difficulties and swallowing issues
* Physiotherapy to address hypotonia and muscle tone concerns
* Behavioural therapy to address developmental and behavioural differences

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may have feeding difficulties, and a small number require longer-term tube feeding.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient took longer to achieve certain developmental milestones like walking and sitting, but once started, progressed well.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and developmental delay is common, ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes asks for repetitions due to not catching what was said the first time, especially with background noise or in a hurry.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia (nearsightedness), noticeable since preschool, and has trouble seeing things far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are prone to cavities due to weak enamel, requiring diligent oral hygiene and regular dental visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth and may experience other dental concerns, including weak enamel.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient takes more time to hit developmental targets than typically expected, which is under observation by her healthcare team.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient took longer to achieve certain developmental milestones but progressed well once started.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, particularly with picking up certain sounds, and has been observed to respond better when speaking directly to him and making sure he can see the speaker's face.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear when she was younger, which was treated, and now her hearing is fine.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which means she needs glasses to see clearly.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, including slower progress in reaching certain milestones like walking or sitting, and is working with a pediatric neurologist to address these delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe, and most people have some element of behavioral differences.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has issues with glue ear, leading to repeated ear infections and some hearing difficulties, and is working with an ENT specialist to manage this condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and many children have required multiple grommet insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tendency to squint, affecting his ability to focus on distant objects, which may impact his learning and overall development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's developmental delays and feeding aversion may impact his learning and educational progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school, and some requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and difficulties with communication, affecting his social interactions and learning processes.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth development and address any dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to assess for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a known structural abnormality in his heart that requires regular monitoring to ensure stability and control.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced significant feeding difficulties in infancy, including trouble latching on and getting frustrated during meal times, although these issues resolved as he grew older.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, including being slower to reach certain milestones like walking or sitting, and has been advised to be given time and space to develop at his own pace.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common in KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe, and most individuals require extra help in school.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to turn the volume of the TV very high, suggesting potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of individuals with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of blurry vision, which may affect his daily activities or learning.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, and may require treatment including patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak teeth, making it challenging to chew harder foods, and requires softer foods or special meal preparation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups, with some needing specialist SEN dentists.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Most individuals with KBG syndrome require extra help in school, with some attending mainstream primary school and others requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and may have behavioural differences, although specific details are not provided.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a noticeably different posture when standing or walking, with a natural lean or bend that doesn't seem typical.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers, and may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on their head or hip dysplasia.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to detect and manage potential hearing issues
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and correct vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor the structural heart abnormality
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any skeletal anomalies

* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and address specific challenges.
